tldr: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on Sep 22, with same-day availability on Amazon Bedrock, and OpenAI answered about an hour later with GPT-6 Sol and Luna. Pricing cuts of 40-50% across vendors followed, and Anthropic then shifted its pitch to cost per task rather than token price.
whats_new: Latent Space reports Opus 5.5 handles explainer-video generation well, an unusually concrete capability read that follows Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 release on AWS on Sep 28.
why_it_matters: Per-token price is no longer the comparison that matters: Anthropic's own cost-per-task analysis shows the same token price can produce very different Claude Code bills depending on settings.

status.detail: Opus 5.5 is generally available on AWS and Anthropic's platform, with Sonnet 5.5 added the following week; independent capability reads are still accumulating.

beats.headline: Opus 5.5 ships on Bedrock the day Anthropic announces it, minutes before GPT-6 Sol and Luna
beats.summary: Anthropic positions Opus 5.5 for agentic coding and long-running tasks; OpenAI releases two GPT-6 models about an hour later.

beats.headline: Vendors cut prices 40-50% and Opus 5.5 becomes AINews's default model
Anthropic argues for cost per task over token price
beats.summary: Two Claude blog posts tie Opus 5.5 pricing to longer, context-heavy coding sessions and show which Claude Code settings change the bill.

beats.headline: Sonnet 5.5 lands on AWS and Opus 5.5 gets its first niche capability read

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm Anthropic's lower cost per task for Opus 5.5 versus GPT-6 Sol?
Do the 40-50% price cuts hold, or are they tied to launch promotions?
Does Sonnet 5.5 undercut Opus 5.5 on cost per task for coding workloads?
take_for_builders: Rerun your own agent workload on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and compare cost per completed task, not cost per token, before changing your default model.
